dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: I see: The flames on the throne have been extinguished, and the burnt ashes have once again turned into trees.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Flowers bloom with your every step, bringing change to an otherwise inevitable decay in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Canotila?

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: #Huh? It's {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}! What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Um, right! The golden butterfly has returned. I need to go and see it! Goodbye!

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Canotila...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: #Huh? {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}... Who are you? I thought no one could get in here besides me.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Wait, how do you know my name?

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Liar! You must be just like those monsters...

choices.text: (Lie) Serene sent me to find you.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Oh... Always making her worry like this, I'm such a bad child...

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: #Right, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}... I remember now... Even though you're a giant monster who could swallow the world in one gulp, you are very kind.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: I saw a few people, but then they slowly melted and turned into monsters...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Since memories can be made into a book, if we reverse that logic, the contents of the book can also be written directly into memories...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Canotila?

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: #Ah, it's you, the strange {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}. What is it? Do you need something from me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What were you talking about...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Hmm. No matter how I think about this, converting memories into a book is quite an incredible deed...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: The creator of this book must've only been able to do this because they viewed the emotions in their memo{RUBY#[D]delusions}ries as the most precious thing in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: That doesn't change how difficult it is to read, though...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: ...And I'm not sure what kind of impact it will have on its readers. This is quite...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Canotila?

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Huh? You're finally back! Don't disappear like that, don't you know how worrying it is? Just imagine what would happen if you never returned...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Do you have any idea how long you were inside? It felt like the waiting would never end... Even the other Melusines had no idea how to help!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It seems like I've been here for quite a while, then.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, I've got to go.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: #What? {NICKNAME}, where are you going...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry. I'll come back once I find you, Canotila.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just wait for me a little longer, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I know that saying this to you won't change much.
